name: Sneeze Tissue
description: A sneezing face with a roll of paper is a runny, messy cold. People send it when the tissues are out, the nose will not stop, and plans are suddenly fragile.
meaning: The sneeze is the symptom and the paper is the supply. Together they mean a cold that is loud, damp, and probably contagious.
examples: this is allergies or a cold and either way 🤧🧻
seoDescription: What does 🤧🧻 mean? A messy cold or allergy attack. The sneeze is the symptom and the paper roll is the evidence.

longForm.overview:
A sneeze and a paper roll are the cold you can hear through a text. 🤧🧻 means tissues are deployed and the sender is leaking, dabbing, and rethinking the afternoon. It covers a virus and it covers a pollen day, which is why some messages shrug and say they do not know which. Readers should treat it as contagious until told otherwise. The paper roll is not decorative. It says the symptom is ongoing, not a single sneeze in a dusty room.

People send the pair to get out of plans without writing a medical essay. They also send it so a video call can stay camera-off without a debate. The tone is miserable and a little comic, because a mountain of tissues is undignified and everyone has been there. Comfort is welcome. Proximity is not. If you were supposed to share a car or a table, assume you are being asked to stay away even if the word "cancel" is only implied by the pictures.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
Morning-of cancellations use 🤧🧻 because it is faster than a paragraph and harder to argue with. Households use it to warn that the tissue box migrated to the couch. Office chats use it as the reason a camera stays off.

Allergy season borrows the same pair, sometimes with a tree emoji elsewhere in the sentence.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not send 🤧🧻 as a fake sick day and then appear at a party. The paper trail of stories will embarrass you more than an honest no.

Skip it to tease someone who sneezed once. A single sneeze is not a cold, and the roll of paper escalates it.
longForm.howToReply:
Release them from the plan and wish the nose well. Offer a drop-off only if you can leave it at the door.

Do not send a home-remedy list. They have tissues. They asked for space or soup, not a clinic.

faqs.question: What does 🤧🧻 mean?
faqs.answer: 🤧🧻 means a runny cold or a bad allergy spell. Tissues are out and the person is probably staying in.

faqs.question: Is 🤧🧻 contagious?
faqs.answer: Assume yes until they say allergies. The pair is a good reason to cancel shared food, cars, and couches.

faqs.question: Does 🤧🧻 always mean a virus?
faqs.answer: No. Pollen produces the same pictures. The careful reply is the same either way: give them the afternoon.

faqs.question: What should I bring someone who sends 🤧🧻?
faqs.answer: Soup or more tissues, left at the door, and only if they want anything. Company is the item they are usually declining.

conversationExamples.message: I am a fountain. 🤧🧻 you do not want this brunch
conversationExamples.interpretation: The brunch seat should be released. Say you will miss them and mean it. Do not ask them to sit at the end of the table anyway.

conversationExamples.message: camera off, mic muted between sentences. 🤧🧻
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are attending while symptomatic and managing the mess. Do not ask them to turn video on for "engagement." Move any discussion that needs their voice.

conversationExamples.message: I was looking forward to tonight and I am 🤧🧻. rain check when I am a person
conversationExamples.interpretation: A date is being postponed for a real reason. Accept it and propose nothing until they say the tissues are gone.

conversationExamples.message: kid is home. couch, cartoons, 🤧🧻. I am next, probably
conversationExamples.interpretation: A household cold is starting. Do not send visitors. Ask what to drop off only if you are already the person who does that.
